artifacts.summary: Verify-and-close-gaps implementation summary: closed the index-entries.json line_count drift, confirmed all seven Phase 3 acceptance criteria as verified no-ops, and recorded the .opencode stale-copy decision (independently-maintained live deliverable, no edit made, follow-up recommended).

completion_data.completion_summary: Verified and closed the one real gap left by the prior over-reaching research dispatch: fixed a line_count drift in agent-system/extensions/web/index-entries.json (110 -> 116) so the web extension passes REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) check-extension-docs.sh. Confirmed all seven acceptance criteria for the Playwright MCP activation as verified no-ops against file contents on disk, and recorded an evidenced decision that .opencode/extensions/web/ is an independently-maintained live deliverable still carrying the stale browser_verify_text_visible reference, out of scope for this task's source-store-only edit rule.

memory_candidates.content: When a doc-lint gate reports a line_count mismatch for a prose file that was just edited (index-entries.json's Rule R check), fix it with a single scoped numeric-field edit at the specific entry, verified with wc -l plus generate-context-line-counts.sh --check (read-only). Never run generate-context-line-counts.sh --write to fix a single-extension drift -- it rewrites line_count across every extension in the repo, producing a large unreviewable diff far outside the task's actual scope.

A misleadingly-titled git commit is not proof of its own claim: a commit titled 'purge .opencode/extensions/{present,web}' in this repo's history in fact touched only 8 unrelated lines of one file and never deleted the directory. When auditing whether a tracked-but-possibly-stale directory (e.g. .opencode/extensions/**, a hand-maintained mirror of agent-system/extensions/**) is a deploy artifact or an independently-maintained deliverable, check three things directly rather than trusting a commit title: (1) whether any live (non-deprecated) deploy script actually writes that path, (2) whether the file's own @-reference convention matches the presumed source (a mismatched reference root like @.opencode/... vs @.claude/... indicates a separately-authored copy, not a generated one), (3) whether git log shows periodic deliberate 'mirror' commits vs automated regeneration commits.
